finding.claim: Tenant wipe has no effective authorization check: requireRole returns a boolean that wipe discards, so any caller can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Any caller reaching Admin.wipe(User u, String tenant), including a user with an empty role set.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive cross-tenant operation.

trace.note: wipe takes the caller User and the target tenant.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") evaluates u.roles().contains("OWNER") and discards the boolean result.

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) is a predicate that returns a boolean and does not throw, so it enforces nothing at the call site. export (line 32) uses checkRole, which throws. No upstream guard is visible in the corpus; the router and auth middleware are not included, so an upstream check cannot be ruled out. Severity held at HIGH; could be CRITICAL if the route is reachable by any authenticated user.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and never throws, and its result is discarded by the bare call at src/Admin.java:26. The only other check in the file, checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22), is used by export (line 32), not wipe. No router, middleware, or auth layer is in the corpus, so none was found.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole and discards its boolean, and src/Admin.java:27 runs repo.wipe(tenant) unconditionally, while the sibling export at line 32 correctly uses the throwing checkRole. The attacker is any caller who reaches the POST /tenants/{t}/wipe handler, and nothing visible blocks that; the one caveat is that the route and auth middleware are outside the corpus, so if an upstream layer restricts the route to OWNER, the severity drops, but the in-file authorization is definitively broken.

finding.claim: Role checks are not bound to the target tenant: a caller who is OWNER of any tenant can export (and wipe) another tenant's data. Conditional on upstream tenant-membership enforcement being absent.
finding.source: A caller holding OWNER in some tenant A, supplying a different tenant B as the argument to Admin.export.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, which exports another tenant's data.

trace.note: User has a flat global roles set with no tenant dimension.
export(User u, String tenant) takes the target tenant from the caller.
checkRole tests only roles().contains("OWNER"), with no tenant argument.
repo.export(tenant) runs for the caller-supplied tenant.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) has no tenant parameter; no membership or ownership lookup appears in export or wipe. The finding closes if the router or repo layer enforces tenant membership, which is outside this corpus. Triage Check 10 (self-affecting only) does not apply because the impact is another tenant's data. Validation Tier 1.

verdict.guard_found: In-file: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws SecurityException on a missing role and its result is not swallowed, but it only tests the global role set and never the tenant. No tenant-membership or ownership check exists in export (src/Admin.java:31-34). The corpus contains only src/Admin.java plus skill docs, so no router or repo-layer tenant check is visible.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: User has only a global roles set (src/Admin.java:4), checkRole tests only "OWNER" with no tenant (src/Admin.java:18-22, 32), and repo.export(tenant) runs with the caller-supplied tenant (src/Admin.java:33). Whether a caller holding OWNER in one tenant can reach another tenant's export depends on tenant-membership enforcement in the router or repo layer, which is not in this corpus, so the finding can be neither confirmed nor refuted from the available code.
